subject: Business
title: The Lean Startup Method
description: A quick win: understand The Lean Startup Method.

hook.text: Eric Ries kept building products nobody wanted. Then he found a faster way to learn.

buildup.text: The lean method says: state a hypothesis, build the smallest test, and measure the result.

discovery.text: This loop — build, measure, learn — replaces months of planning with weeks of real evidence.

twist.text: Most founders skip 'measure' and jump from building to building. Speed without learning is waste.

climax.text: Dropbox didn't build a product first. They posted a demo video and measured signups.

punchline.text: The goal isn't shipping fast. It's learning fast.

quiz.question: What is the core loop of the Lean Startup method?

details.summary: Eric Ries's Lean Startup methodology replaces traditional business planning with iterative build-measure-learn cycles that validate assumptions through experiments.
details.whyItMatters: The Lean Startup changed how companies are built worldwide. By treating every startup assumption as a hypothesis to test rather than a truth to execute, it dramatically reduced the waste of building products nobody wants and shortened the path to
takeaways: Replace lengthy business plans with rapid build-measure-learn experiments
Every assumption is a hypothesis to test, not a truth to execute on blind faith
Validated learning through experiments is the true measure of startup progress

faq.question: What is the core difference between lean startup and traditional startup approaches?
faq.answer: Traditional approaches assume the business plan is correct and focus on execution. Lean startup assumes everything is uncertain and focuses on learning what customers actually want through rapid experiments. Progress is measured by validated learning, not by milestones on a plan.

faq.question: What are the limitations of the lean startup approach?
faq.answer: Some products require significant upfront investment before any version is viable. Deep tech and hardware are harder to iterate quickly. Over-indexing on current customer feedback can prevent visionary products. The lean approach works best for software and digital services with low iteration costs.
